issue_context.title: Change Insight.Group return type to IEnumerable<Insight> from Guid
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
Get `IEnumerable<Insight>` from `Insight.Group(params Insight[])` call.

#### Actual Behavior
`Insight.Group(params Insight[])` returns the Guid that was assigned to the group members.

#### Potential Solution
Change return type.

#### Checklist
- [x] I have completely filled out this template
- [x] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch
- [x] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues)

review_comments: Is this necessary? The `params` modifier should do this by default? Is this added for python convenience?

Yes. This is due to pythonnet inability to solve this:
```python
Insight.Group(insight)
```
as it says that it cannot find an overload. 
I could take a look at pythonnet and solve this issue.

But is that required? a Group method for one insight? I think all other places we use C# `params` we use python `[]` array notation. I'm not against adding this, just wondering if it adds much value, that's all.
